answer.label: In short
answer.lead: D2C food and beverage marketing is the work of winning first orders for products with low basket values, then earning reorders quickly. It covers taste-led creative, bundles that lift order value, marketplace and quick commerce presence, and reminders timed to when a pack runs out.
answer.who: Monday Marketing Company (MMC) markets D2C food and beverage brands in India across creative, own site, marketplaces, quick commerce and retention.

answer.chip: Low basket, high repeat, planned for both

blocks.h: How food and drink gets bought
paras: Buyers try a food or drink on impulse or a recommendation, judge it on taste and reorder if it fits a habit. Many shop on quick commerce and marketplaces, where a listing and its availability matter as much as an ad.
Shelf life, packaging and delivery condition also affect trust and returns.
blocks.cap: Illustrative scene: a product listing on a quick commerce app.

blocks.h: The problem that keeps coming back
paras: A low basket value has to cover product, packing, delivery and acquisition. Many food brands win a first order at a loss and never earn it back.
The fix is order value and reorder: bundles, subscriptions and reminders. We read it with the free tools and the guides.

callout.title: Rules apply to food.
callout.text: Labelling and health claims are regulated. We use only claims you can document.

leaks.eyebrow: Where food and beverage marketing leaks
leaks.lede: Each stage below is where a food brand loses margin or a reorder, and the work that fixes it.

stages.why: Food is bought with the eyes. A plain pack shot does not say how it tastes or when to eat it.
stages.does: We shoot and edit short video around taste, use and occasion. See UGC and video.

stages.breaks: Selling one low-price item at a time.
stages.why: A single low-price order rarely pays for acquisition and shipping.
stages.does: We build bundles, trial packs and thresholds that raise order value without eroding margin. See CRO.

stages.k: Be on the shelves buyers use
stages.why: Many buyers open a quick commerce app or marketplace before a brand site.
stages.does: We run listings, availability and ads there. See quick commerce and Amazon Ads.

stages.breaks: Chasing ROAS on a thin margin.
stages.why: With low baskets, small errors in cost assumptions turn a profitable campaign into a loss.
stages.does: We set targets from full unit economics and run Meta and Google against them.

stages.why: Food is a habit product. Timing the reminder to when a pack runs out captures reorders.
stages.does: We set reorder flows and subscriptions by pack size. See retention.
